picked.t: Vietnam adds two paid public holidays, brings annual total to 13
picked.body: The National Assembly on Saturday passed legislation amending and supplementing several articles of the Labor Code. Under the revised legislation, workers will receive two additional paid days off: July 27, observed as Invalids and Martyrs' Day, and Nov. 24, designated as Vietnam Culture Day. The new holiday provisions will take effect on different dates. Vietnam Culture Day will become a public holiday in 2026, while Invalids and Martyrs' Day will be added from 2027 The amended law is scheduled to take effect on March 1, 2027. With the additions, Vietnam will have 13 paid public holidays annually. These include five days for the Lunar New Year ( Tet ), two days for National Day, and one day each for New Year's Day, the Hung Kings' Commemoration Day, Reunification Day (April 30), and International Workers' Day (May 1). The proposal to make July 27 a public holiday was first put forward by the Government during the 2019 revision of the Labor Code but was not adopted at the time. The proposal being incorporated into law recognizes the contributions and sacrifices of those who served the nation and reinforcing Vietnam’s tradition of gratitude to those who made sacrifices for its independence and development. The legislation also requires the Minister of Home Affairs to announce the following year’s public holiday and Tet schedules by Sept. 30 each year, based on a decision by the Prime Minister.

picked.t: Vietnam's largest airport Long Thanh to open with flights to Hanoi
picked.body: The Airports Corporation of Vietnam (ACV), the airport's developer, said on Saturday it is working with authorities to complete licensing for the first commercial flights, which are scheduled to begin at midnight on Dec. 24. Vietnam Airlines plans to operate flights on the airport's first day. The carrier has sent ACV its initial schedule and plans two test flights in December before regular operations begin. It has registered 28 flights a week, or four a day, on the Long Thanh-Hanoi route. Vietjet plans to bring one Airbus A321 to Long Thanh on Dec. 24 to fly the Hanoi route. In the second week, it will add a second aircraft and open routes to Hai Phong and Vinh. By mid-January 2027, Vietjet expects to station a third aircraft at the airport, expanding its Long Thanh network to Hanoi, Hai Phong, Vinh, Da Nang, Hue, Thanh Hoa and Phu Quoc. Based on the takeoff and landing slots the airlines have registered, ACV expects Long Thanh to handle up to 226 flights a week in the initial phase, which runs until March 27, 2027. Domestic routes operated by Vietnam Airlines and Vietjet account for up to 182 of them. That is down from the up to 366 flights a week ACV projected for the initial phase in late October. On international routes, Vietnam Airlines is the first carrier to register at Long Thanh, with 44 flights a week, up to eight a day, to Beijing, Guangzhou, Hong Kong and Manila. 34 foreign airlines have asked to dely their move from Tan Son Nhat Airport in Ho Chi Minh City to Long Thanh until 2027 winter to enable more preparation. ACV and the airlines will update the official flight schedule in early December, once the remaining procedures are completed. The airport will initially prioritize domestic and short-haul international routes. From April 2027, it will move into its next operating phase, with traffic rising in line with the summer schedule. ACV and its contractors are now finishing construction, installing equipment and carrying out acceptance checks and trial runs of the airport's systems to prepare for passengers. Located in Dong Nai City, about 40 km east of Ho Chi Minh City's Tan Son Nhat Airport, Long Thanh is Vietnam's largest airport by area, covering about 5,000 hectares, with a planned total investment of nearly $16 billion. Its first phase is designed to handle 25 million passengers and 1.2 million tons of cargo a year.

picked.t: 3 more execs resign from Vietnam’s largest listed jewelry company PNJ
picked.body: Dao Trung Kien is senior director of strategy and performance management, and holds a 0.08% stake in the company, Nguyen Chi Kien (0.03% stake) is senior director of human resources, and Truong Hoai Anh (0.06%) is senior director of customer relations and retail. The company said they had asked to step down for "personal reasons." The latest departures will bring to four the number of senior executives to quit in less than three weeks from the company’s finance, strategy, human resources, and customer relations and retail departments. Nguyen Minh Hai had stepped down as senior director of finance on Nov. 17 also for personal reasons. PNJ has appointed Diep My Tam Xuan to succeed Nguyen Anh Tuan as head of internal audit. Tuan became deputy head. The changes follow a reorganization at the jeweler, which adopted a new corporate structure on Oct. 10. PNJ had more than 7,100 employees at the end of September, down by more than 1,000 from the end of the second quarter. It operates over 400 stores. The company has faced difficulties since July, when news broke that police had arrested Dang Ngoc Thao, the former director of PNJ’s gem-testing subsidiary P-Lab, in connection with a ring that smuggled diamonds from Hong Kong into Vietnam. The police have said, however, that most of the 30,000 smuggled diamonds were not distributed through PNJ stores. The reports brought customers rushing to sell back diamonds and jewelry they had bought to PNJ. In July alone, buybacks totaled nearly VND6 trillion, almost as much as in all of 2025. By the end of that quarter, the total commitments to buy back or exchange those products was estimated at VND21 trillion (US$813.75 million). Diamonds and diamond jewelry accounted for 52% of PNJ’s total inventory . At an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting in October, PNJ approved a plan to set aside VND7.07 trillion to cover losses related to its buyback and exchange policy. It also plans to issue 550 million shares through a private placement to raise VND8 trillion to rebuild the business. PNJ expects a record loss of VND6.27 trillion this year. It posted a loss of nearly VND258 billion in the third quarter.
